title: Rare Annapurna Darshan Opens in Kashi for Dhanteras and Diwali 2026
excerpt: The special murti at Varanasi's Annapurna Temple, beside Kashi Vishwanath, is open only around Dhanteras and Annakut — November 6 to 11 in 2026, with Annakut on November 10.
body:
• The special murti of Goddess Annapurna in Varanasi, beside the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, can be seen only around Dhanteras and Annakut — in 2026 the temple window runs November 6 to 11, with Annakut on November 10, according to Hindu Blog.
  • Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, 2026, and Diwali (Lakshmi Puja) on Sunday, November 8, 2026 — devotees planning a Kashi trip should build it around those dates, not a later Diwali date.
  • Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple opens daily at 2:30 a.m. and closes at 11 p.m., with general darshan from 4 to 11 a.m. and from noon to 7 p.m., according to the temple trust's official portal.

For a few days around Diwali, Varanasi offers a darshan that is not available at any other time of year. The Annapurna Temple in Varanasi, dedicated to Goddess Annapurna and located beside the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, houses a unique murti of the goddess that devotees can see only on Dhanteras and Annakut day, Hindu Blog reports. In 2026, it says, the temple is open from November 6 to November 11, and Annakut is on November 10.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 (Dhanteras) to Wednesday, November 11, 2026; Annakut on Tuesday, November 10, 2026; Diwali on Sunday, November 8, 2026
  • Venue: Annapurna Temple, Varanasi, beside the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple
  • Time: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple opens 2:30 a.m., closes 11 p.m.; general darshan 4–11 a.m. and noon–7 p.m. (temple trust schedule)
  • Contact: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust, Goyanka Bhawan, Varanasi-221 001; Ph: 0542-2392629
  • Official page: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple rituals and timings

What makes this darshan rare

Hindu Blog explains that the temple houses murtis of Goddess Annapurna, Vishwanath, Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi, and that a distinctive feature of the Annapurna and Shiva murtis is that Shiva is depicted as receiving alms from the goddess. On Annakut day, 56 types of food are offered to the deities, including fruits, sweets, boiled rice and pulses, placed in front of the deities so that it forms a mountain, and later distributed as prasad. Devotees observe a complete fast on Annakut day, the report adds. In Kashi, unlike in Dwarka and Krishna temples where Annakut is dedicated to Krishna, the observance is dedicated to Goddess Annapurna.

The wider Kashi Vishwanath complex marks the same festival window. A syndicated report on Devdiscourse described a six-day Deep Jyoti Mahotsav beginning at the Kashi Vishwanath Dham on Dhanteras, with the shrine decorated with flowers and lights and the Annapurna temple inside the complex also decked up. On Diwali night, the temple premises are illuminated with diyas, and the next observance, Annakoot Mahotsav, sees 56 varieties of offerings presented to Lord Vishwanath and Ma Annapurna, the Dham's chief executive said in that report.

"In 2026, it says, the temple is open from November 6 to November 11, and Annakut is on November 10."

The dates to plan around in 2026

The festival calendar for 2026 is: Dhanteras on Friday, November 6; Diwali and Lakshmi Puja on Sunday, November 8; Govardhan Puja and Annakut on Tuesday, November 10; and Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, November 11, according to a Diwali 2026 calendar guide. That sequence is why the Annapurna temple window and Annakut fall where they do this year: Annakut is observed on Kartik Shukla Paksha Pratipada, the first day of the waxing phase of the moon in Kartik, Hindu Blog notes.

Planning a visit

Pair the rare Annapurna darshan with darshan at Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple itself. The temple trust's official rituals page states the temple opens daily at 2:30 a.m., Mangala Aarti is performed from 3 to 4 a.m. for ticket holders, general darshan runs from 4 to 11 a.m., Mid-Day Bhog Aarti is performed from 11:30 a.m. to noon, darshan resumes from noon to 7 p.m., Sapta Rishi Aarti runs from 7 to 8:30 p.m., Shayan Aarti starts at 10:30 p.m. and the temple closes at 11 p.m. Festival-day arrangements can differ from the daily schedule, so check the official portal before travelling. For diaspora visitors timing a trip home for Diwali, the practical window is tight: arrive before November 6 if Dhanteras darshan is the goal, and stay through November 10 for Annakut.
